chunks: As for the good government, the pious man performs good acts in it, and as for the bad government, the wicked person enjoys in it, until his term ends and death overtakes him.

key_terms.الشَّقِيُّ: The happy, fortunate, or wicked person (who enjoys)
key_terms.الْبَرَّةُ: Good, virtuous, or righteous (referring to the government)
key_terms.الْفَاجِرَةُ: Bad, wicked, or corrupt (referring to the government)

ai.seo_question: How do the pious and the wicked experience good versus bad government according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In his response to the Kharijite slogan 'Judgment belongs to God alone,' Imam Ali clarifies that divine decree operates through human agency and governance; the righteous (al-Taqi) actively cultivate virtue within the existing political order, while the wicked (al-Shaqi) reap worldly benefits despite its flaws. This highlights the Shia principle of pragmatic engagement with authority, where the pious do not withdraw from society but use the prevailing conditions to accumulate spiritual merit until death concludes their earthly tenure.
